$comment: Batch 4 — token. The six S/add-token states, from the reach steps an earlier agent verified against the running app. GROUP ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: the ERC-20 lane runs before the native lane because `vela.clear()` in erc20-resolved wipes the faults, and the native lane needs none.
$why-no-sheet-states: O/add-token-sheet/{resolving,resolved,error} are NOT boarded. AddTokenSheet.tsx is a stateless wrapper — 66 lines, zero useState: <AppModal> + a close header + <AddTokenPanel>. Every state it can show is a state of the panel, which the six boards below already depict. Boarding them again would put the same picture in the file under a second name, which is the defect this project has been fixing all day.

states.note: the address is being looked up across every chain: the field is frozen and the CTA carries a spinner while each network is tried in turn
the token resolved: its symbol, name, decimals and the chain it was found on, in a result card above the confirm action
states.$why-the-wait: a dead chain burns three attempts of eight seconds each before the lookup settles, so this beat is ~42s after the fault is cleared. It is a wait, not a race.

states.note: no chain knows this address — the panel raises the not-found alert over itself rather than clearing the field, so the address stays editable
a chain has been picked from the suggestions and its compatibility is being checked — the 4337 stack has to exist on it before the wallet can offer it
the chain carries the EntryPoint and the Safe factory: the wallet can be used there, and the panel says so before the user commits
states.$why-weak-expect: 'Celo' is present at network-checking too, so it cannot discriminate. What separates the two is the verdict row appearing; differsFrom against the checking beat is the assertion that actually holds, and the forbid catches the incompatible branch landing here by mistake.

states.$why-zksync: zkSync 324, not Celo — Celo resolves COMPATIBLE. The incompatible branch needs a chain whose 4337 stack is genuinely absent.
states.note: the chain has no 4337 stack, so the wallet cannot operate there — the panel refuses and explains, rather than adding a network that would fail at the first send
states.$why-own-group: a fresh /add-token load. Inside the native group the panel has already consumed its tab: after a chain is picked there is no 'Native Token' control left to click, so the step found no element — loudly, which is the harness working.
states.$why-the-forbid: the assertion that was missing. The earlier recipe used zkSync 324 on an agent's say-so and asserted only that the dump contained '324' and differed from its sibling — both true of the COMPATIBLE verdict, which is what zkSync returns today. The board would have claimed to show a chain the wallet cannot use while showing 'Compatible · Add Network'. Differing from a sibling is not the same as being right.
